title: Ops Thermograph: surge gauges and thermal health controls for Dedicated capacity
creator: Asha Menon
description: Design a compact, glanceable "thermograph" component and a set of surge gauges to surface GPU pool thermal health, burst headroom, autoscale tension, and cost risk for Dedicated clusters. Targets operators and platform engineers who need to decide whether to allow bursts, trigger scale actions, or initiate fallbacks.
design_notes: Goals: 1) Provide a single-line summary (Thermal Index) with three micro-gauges (Burst Headroom, Autoscale Tension, Cost Risk). 2) Allow inline actions: toggle burst allowance, open canary rollout, open autoscale editor, and quick link to detailed timeline. 3) Support per-pool and per-tenant modes. 4) Ensure compactness for table rows and expanded card for deep-dive. Consider color-blind palettes, aria labels for gauges, and motion reduced state for animations.
acceptance_criteria: Thermograph component renders in pool list with a 48px-high compact row and expands to a 320x180 card on click
Burst Headroom gauge calculates using free GPU memory + queued requests and renders numeric + color band (green/yellow/red)
Autoscale Tension shows current policy margin and time-to-provision estimate; editable via inline pencil action that opens autoscale editor modal
Cost Risk gauge projects 24h estimated extra cost for current burst settings and links to cost preview page
All micro-interactions accessible with keyboard and labelled for screen readers
Figma prototype linked and annotated; design sign-off from PM and Eng leads recorded
review_feedback: PM: Prefer explicit numeric tooltip for 'time-to-provision' rather than only percentile bands
Eng: Need API contract for 'thermal_index' and 'burst_headroom' fields; discuss rounding and sample window (30s vs 60s)
Security: Ensure quick-action toggles require RBAC check and record audit events
Design: Replace red-only band with patterned fill when user has motion reduced preference
Accessibility: Provide textual fallback in export/CSV for gauge values
decisions: Use unified Thermal Index (0-100) combining temp, queue, and eviction risk; color stops at 40/70
Compact mode will show icons + microbars; expand will show mini-graphs of 5m, 1h windows
Burst toggle will be soft by default and require explicit confirmation for high-cost pools
Autoscale editor will reuse existing autoscale modal (console-autoscale-v2) to reduce duplicate UX
next_steps: Add ENG dependency: ENG-22418 to define runtime metric stream and endpoint
Hand off annotated Figma frames + component spec to front-end (deadline 2025-11-21)
Create GH issue with implementation checklist and accessibility test cases
